environment.platform: KVM VM (qemu, 4 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM) running Fedora 42 Cloud, kind v0.33.0 cluster
environment.cgroup: cgroup2fs (unified); cgroup v1 unavailable, so release_agent technique was not runnable

primitives.name: core_pattern overwrite
primitives.raw_event: process_exec for /bin/sh present in base sensor; write syscall present in kernel
primitives.baseline_alert: NO - policy openat path selector did not match; no alert emitted

primitives.name: modprobe_path overwrite
primitives.raw_event: process_exec for /bin/sh present in base sensor; write syscall present in kernel
primitives.baseline_alert: NO - policy openat path selector did not match; no alert emitted

primitives.name: bind-mount /proc/1/root
primitives.baseline_alert: YES (unconditional mount kprobe; no path discrimination)

primitives.name: post-exec capset
primitives.status: FAIL (busybox setpriv syntax; syscall not exercised as intended)
primitives.raw_event: process_kprobe __x64_sys_capset events present from container runtime processes

primitives.name: post-exec setuid(0) then core_pattern write (stale credential)
primitives.raw_event: process_exec recorded uid=1000; process_lsm alert for the write also recorded uid=1000
primitives.baseline_alert: NO (policy keyed on user.uid=0 would see uid=1000 in the event)
primitives.fixed_alert: YES (LSM file_open guard fires, but with stale uid=1000 attribute)

notes: No exploit code was used; primitives are configuration/syscall actions in a privileged pod.
The triple (raw event, alert, success) is captured per primitive from agent JSON logs and pod stdout.
P1/P2 demonstrate the observed-but-not-detected gap on a real agent: syscall visible, no baseline alert.
The fixed detector adds an LSM file_open guard that restores alerts for P1/P2.
release_agent (cgroup v1) could not be executed: this VM and kernel provide only cgroup v2.

benign_workload.description: ~40 s of genuine workload in the VM: 100 nginx HTTP requests plus 100 gcc compile-and-run cycles and normal shell/file commands
benign_workload.note: The 14 alerts come from unconditional kprobes (setuid/capset/mount/setns/bpf) that also fire on benign system activity; the LSM guard produced zero false positives.

attack_run.note: The 954 kprobe alerts in the window are dominated by container-runtime processes; only 827 are attributable to the attacker pod binaries.

overhead.benchmark: 20,000,000 getpid(2) calls in a tight C loop on the VM host, 3 repetitions, wall-clock seconds
overhead.relative_overhead: ~0.6%, within run-to-run variation; the loaded hooks do not fire on getpid

race_poc_attempt.method: setuid-root helper binary executed by uid 1000 in a privileged pod; setuid(0) after exec; write to /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern
race_poc_attempt.result: PoC shows uid 1000 at exec and uid 0 at write; Tetragon process_exec and the LSM alert both record uid=1000 (exec-time snapshot), proving the telemetry attribute is stale.

multiagent.note: Stock configurations of all three agents observed the workload but produced no escape-specific alert for the two successful host-config writes; a two-rule LSM guard added to Tetragon restored detection.

tetragon.policy: custom 7-hook escape-observe (+ LSM guard in fix experiment)
tetragon.result: 423 kprobe alerts; LSM guard produced 4 attacker-attributable alerts on core_pattern/modprobe in the fix experiment

falco.result: 3 alerts, all "Executing binary not part of base image" on mount/umount; no escape-specific alert for core_pattern/modprobe writes

tracee.result: 10 security_file_open events; no core_pattern_modification detector event observed for the writes
